items.title: Albert Warner Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: Me, I've tried my whole life to try and make him learn how to read like I could.

ctx.x: No, no. I don't know. Wait, wait, wait a minute. It looks that way. Wait, wait, wait a minute. Goddamn. I couldn't talk once. I couldn't talk once. I had a much. How can I teach when I taught? I couldn't talk once. But, let me tell you, kid. He said, sometime, when he and I get together, I said, I said, I said, partner? I said, I said, I'm learning how to talk good. He gave me a lesson. He said, I'll find him out sometime, you see. Well, they did tell me that Sonny was Jim's uncle.
I'm the teacher. Jim's uncle though. No.

Uncle? No, we used to know him. You did know him, of course, down in the country. Yeah, I know him so long. I know him, I understand, first. I didn't know him. I think he's teacher. But sometimes he would get to talk. I said, partner, I said, you are learning good how to talk. I said, just keep on using it.
